ayahs.1: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.3: And what will make you realize what the Inevitable Hour is?
ayahs.4: Thamud and Ad denied the Striking Disaster.
ayahs.5: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by an overwhelming blast.
ayahs.6: As for Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, bitter wind
ayahs.7: that Allah unleashed on them non-stop for seven nights and eight days, so you would have seen its people lying dead like trunks of uprooted palm trees.
ayahs.8: Do you see any of them left alive?
ayahs.9: Pharaoh and those before him, and the overturned cities of Lot, indulged in sin,
ayahs.10: each disobeying their Lord's messenger, so He seized them with a crushing grip.
ayahs.11: When the floodwater overflowed, We carried you in the floating Ark with Noah,
ayahs.12: so that We might make this a reminder for you, and that attentive ears may grasp it.
ayahs.13: When the Trumpet is blown with one blast,
ayahs.14: and the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with one blow,
ayahs.15: on that Day the Inevitable Event will have come to pass.
ayahs.16: The sky will be torn and become frail,
ayahs.17: with the angels on its sides. On that Day eight mighty angels will bear the Throne of your Lord above them.
ayahs.18: You will be presented for judgment, and none of your secrets will stay hidden.
ayahs.19: Those given their record in their right hand will cry happily: 'Here, everyone! Read my record!'
ayahs.20: I surely knew I would face my reckoning.'
ayahs.21: They will be in a life of bliss,
ayahs.23: whose fruit will hang within reach.
ayahs.24: They will be told: 'Eat and drink joyfully for what you did in the days gone by.'
ayahs.25: Those given their record in their left hand will cry bitterly: 'I wish I had not been given my record,
ayahs.26: nor known anything of my reckoning!
ayahs.27: I wish death had been the end!
ayahs.28: My wealth has not benefited me!
ayahs.29: My authority has been stripped from me.'
ayahs.30: It will be said: 'Seize and shackle them,
ayahs.32: then tie them with chains seventy arms long.
ayahs.33: For they never had iman in Allah, the Greatest,
ayahs.35: So this Day they will have no close friend here,
ayahs.36: nor any food except oozing pus,
ayahs.37: which none will eat except the evildoers.'
ayahs.38: Now I swear by whatever you see
ayahs.40: This Quran is the recitation of a noble Messenger.
ayahs.41: It is not the prose of a poet, yet you hardly have any faith.
ayahs.42: Nor is it the mumbling of a fortune-teller, yet you are hardly mindful.
ayahs.43: It is a revelation from the Lord of all worlds.
ayahs.44: Had the Messenger invented something in Our Name,
ayahs.45: We would have seized him by his right hand,
ayahs.47: and none of you could have shielded him from Us.
ayahs.48: This Quran is a reminder for those living with taqwa—Allah-consciousness.
ayahs.49: We know that some of you will persist in denial,
ayahs.50: and it will surely be a source of regret for the those who reject the truth.
ayahs.51: This Quran is the absolute truth.
ayahs.52: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Greatest.
